newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Delta sees no reason to hedge platinum.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Delta sees no reason to hedge platinum.

text.p: Delta Gold NL said on Wednesday it sees no reason yet to hedge forward its share of future production of platinum from the Hartley platinum project in Zimbabwe.
"There's no immediate imperative or incentive to hedge," Fiona Robertson, general manager of finance for Delta, told a press briefing.
The individual prices for the basket of metals to be produced from the Hartley project tend to move out of tandem, reducing overall volatility, Robertson said.

Hartley is scheduled to start production in June 1997 at an annual rate of around 150,000 ounces of platinum, 115,000 ounces of palladium, 11,500 ounces of rhodium and 23,000 ounces of gold, as well as some copper and nickel.

"In the platium and platinum group metals markets, you don't get the forward contangos that you get in the gold market. So there's much less incentive to sell forward to earn the contango than you have in the gold market currently," Robertson said.
Russian stockpiles of palladium are sufficient to last a further three to five years at the current rate of exports, Delta's chairman, Peter Vanderspuy, told the briefing.
Industry studies suggest about half the estimated 4.2 million ounces of palladium exported by Russia last year came from stockpiles, Vanderspuy said.
He said world demand for palladium was probably around 6.1 million ounces in 1995.
Delta said earlier on Wednesday that delays in commissioning of a processing plant at the Hartley project would not affect plans to bring the operation into full production on schedule.
Delta holds a 33 percent interest in the project, with The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd holding the rest.
